name: pin-drag
about: Puppet pins under the hand (Q239): the same character and the same wrist arc as pose-drag, driven by a pin instead of a bone, so the two scenarios are one comparison. The fixture carries three pins already dropped — shoulder [0.35, 0.5], elbow [0.5, 0.5], wrist [0.65, 0.5] — because dropping a pin is a different cost (pin.prepare: meshing the drawing and factorising, paid once) from dragging one (pin.solve: per pointer event). Measures pin.drag (the UI cost of each pointer batch), pin.solve, pin.frame (the posed drawing's geometry through the mesh), the re-stamp, time to screen, and pin.commit. Then drops a fourth pin mid-forearm to put one pin.prepare on the record, and undoes everything. The acceptance line is in docs/DESIGN-puppet-pins.md: no metric here more than 15% above its pose-drag counterpart, and no stall either scenario does not have.
